claims.title: Exact Le Cam deficiency of a visibility-contracted Bell simulator with equal correlation magnitudes: delta = C(1 - lam)/(2(2 - C lam)), also against arbitrary kernels on the joint record under schedule averaging
claims.scope: one-trial fixed-phase visibility family P_v(a,b|i) = (1 + v ab c_i)/4, v in [0,1], |c_i| = C for every setting pair, simulator P_{lam v}; setting-preserving kernels under schedule-average or worst-setting TV, and arbitrary Markov kernels on the joint (setting, outcome) record under schedule-average TV
assumptions: the setting pair is public and the kernel may depend on it
lam in [0,1] is fixed and known
TV is half the L1 distance
the post-processing is central: it sees both settings and both outcomes; it is not restricted to Bell-local (LOSR) operations
every setting pair has the same correlation magnitude C in [0,1] and the schedule has full support
nonclaims: deficiency, the Le Cam distance and the randomization criterion are classical (Le Cam 1964, 1986); after the endpoint and sufficiency reductions the value is a deficiency between Bernoulli dichotomies governed by Torgersen's dichotomy theory (Torgersen 1970, 1991); only the closed form for this Bell family and its packaging are claimed
the value is not claimed for schedule-averaged TV with unequal correlation magnitudes (ST-O08)
deficiency under Bell-local (LOSR) post-processing is not computed; it is at least delta, and a float LP probe during review (not a certificate) gave 0.136730 versus 0.107369 at canonical lam = 1/2
the n-trial product-experiment deficiency is not computed
small deficiency does not imply identical implementation and is not evidence about simulation

claims.title: Worst-setting deficiency for unequal magnitudes: delta = V(max_i |c_i|) with V(C) = C(1 - lam)/(2(2 - C lam))
claims.scope: the declared interface with arbitrary finite magnitudes |c_i| under worst-setting aggregation
assumptions: the setting pair is public and the kernel may depend on it
lam in [0,1] is fixed and known
TV is half the L1 distance
the post-processing is central: it sees both settings and both outcomes; it is not restricted to Bell-local (LOSR) operations
worst-setting aggregation
nonclaims: no statement for schedule-averaged TV with unequal magnitudes (ST-O08)

claims.title: (standard) Risk transfer: |risk gap| <= 2 delta ||L|| for every bounded loss and decision rule, tight under equal magnitudes
claims.scope: every bounded-loss decision problem on the declared interface; tightness under equal magnitudes with delta from ST-T306 (a decision may depend on the setting)
assumptions: the setting pair is public and the kernel may depend on it
lam in [0,1] is fixed and known
TV is half the L1 distance
the post-processing is central: it sees both settings and both outcomes; it is not restricted to Bell-local (LOSR) operations
losses are bounded and decision rules act on the post-processed record
equal magnitudes for the tightness statement
nonclaims: a direct instance of Le Cam's randomization criterion (Le Cam 1964; Torgersen 1991), not new
with unequal magnitudes the bound 2 delta_max ||L|| holds but is not claimed tight
risk transfer is uniform over v in [0,1] on this interface only; no statement about decision problems that see hidden implementation variables

claims.title: Deterministic setting-wise relabelings cannot match the randomized deficiency of a visibility-contracted Bell simulator for 0 < C < 1 (worst setting also at C = 1, 0 < lam < 1)
claims.scope: deterministic setting-preserving relabelings of the equal-magnitude visibility family; the dominating set {A,B,D} of per-setting error pairs over all (C,lam) in [0,1]^2 via an exact arrangement-vertex certificate; worst-setting value min(C(1-lam)/2,1/4); schedule-averaged lower bound along the segment AD; strict gap for 0 < C < 1 and 0 <= lam < 1
assumptions: the setting pair is public and the kernel may depend on it
lam in [0,1] is fixed and known
TV is half the L1 distance
the post-processing is central: it sees both settings and both outcomes; it is not restricted to Bell-local (LOSR) operations
each setting's kernel is a 0/1 relabeling of that setting's outcomes with no auxiliary randomness (setting-preserving)
the dominating-set step is a computer-assisted exact proof: exact rational evaluation at all arrangement vertices, covering all parameters by piecewise linearity
nonclaims: deterministic maps that may relabel the setting on the joint record are not covered; they can beat delta_hull (23/160 < 3/14 on the rational schedule at lam = 1/4); whether they can reach delta is open
no strict schedule-averaged gap is claimed at C = 1
with an admitted auxiliary random coin the deterministic and randomized values coincide

the general separation between information and randomization resources is classical in spirit (Blackwell 1951; Le Cam 1964) and is recorded in ST-T174; only the explicit frontier and values for this family are claimed

claims.title: Exact deficiency audit on canonical CHSH, a rational schedule, a setting-relabeling map, and an unequal-magnitude schedule
claims.scope: canonical uniform CHSH (C = 1/sqrt2, exact in Q(sqrt2)) and C = 3/5 with weights (1/2,1/4,1/8,1/8), lam in {k/8}, v grid {k/10}; joint-kernel dual; the joint deterministic map at lam = 1/4; c = (1/2,-1/10,3/5) under worst-setting aggregation
assumptions: exact Fraction and Q(sqrt2) arithmetic; no floating-point line is part of the receipt
nonclaims: the averaged deterministic values are certified only on the listed schedules and grid
